bg.purpose: The page ground. Warm off-white, never a true white.

surface.purpose: Cards, panels, and every resting control.

surface-2.purpose: Subtle insets, secondary panels, hover fills, chip grounds.

surface-3.purpose: Stronger insets, disabled fills, active filter chips.

accent.purpose: The brand accent. Fills that carry NO text.

accent-solid.purpose: The only accent fill that carries text. Pairs with Clay Ink.

accent-ink.purpose: Accent text on a neutral background. NOT text-on-accent.

accent-fg.purpose: Ink for text on Clay Solid. 5.02:1 light / 6.49:1 dark.

ok.purpose: Success. Also the Хорошо grade fill.

warn.purpose: Warning — fill only. 3.16:1 as text; use warn-text.

danger.purpose: Error / destructive. Also the Снова grade fill.

display.purpose: The Kazakh word, and page headings. The only place the product shows a second voice.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: The faintest lift; disabled and inert states.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: The resting flashcard. Also the anchor of the card-landing animation.

motion.name: dur-press
motion.purpose: The control acknowledging the finger. Under 150ms reads as physical.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: A routine state change: hover, colour, a row settling.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: An overlay or a state swap: a modal, a toast, the scrim.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: The authored moment — the card landing. Reserved on purpose.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Loops that go out and come back (shimmer, audio pulse).

motion.name: ease-linear
motion.purpose: Continuous rotation only. Any easing on a spinner reads as stutter.

motion.name: card-land
motion.purpose: The flashcard lands: shadow tightens onto an opaque surface, no fade.

breakpoints.name: nav-drawer
breakpoints.purpose: Load-bearing: swaps the inline nav for the burger drawer. Raised from 540px — the full header row needs ~890px, so between 541 and ~890 it overflowed the viewport (measured 864px of content in an 844px landscape phone, on every page).

breakpoints.name: touch-floor
breakpoints.purpose: The gate for --tap-min and for the compact study layout. The same query is COMPACT_QUERY in StudyPage.tsx so the JSX and CSS cannot drift.

breakpoints.name: study-short
breakpoints.purpose: Landscape phone: splits the study screen into controls left, card and answer right.

knownDebt: No spacing token scale. 27 distinct px values are in use in padding/margin; the rhythm is a loose 2px step with a 4px preference, clustering on 4/6/8/10/12/14/16/20/24/32px.
Breakpoints are not unified — the map is now seven max-width values plus two height queries and the touch gate. Only the touch gate and the landscape split are load-bearing across modules.
The mobile nav drawer opens and closes with no transition; it is the only overlay not using the shared arrival vocabulary.
On the study screen at desktop width the undo toast overlaps the "Показать ответ" button.
The main study view renders no <h1> — only the done state has one. The .studyTitle class still exists in StudyPage.module.css and is rendered by nothing.

components.name: Button — Primary
components.description: The one solid accent surface. Carries the page's primary action; text is Clay Ink on Clay Solid, never white on bare Clay.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary" type="button">Начать с A1 <svg class="ds-ico" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><line x1="5" x2="19" y1="12" y2="12"/><polyline points="12 5 19 12 12 19"/></svg></button>

components.name: Button — Ghost
components.description: The default for every secondary action: a hairline and ink, no fill. Hover adds a tinted ground rather than colour.

components.name: SM-2 Rating Button — resting
components.description: The study screen's signature control. Neutral surface; the state is carried by a 1px keyline and the label colour, never by the fill. The shortcut chip inherits the label colour.
components.notes: No :hover here on purpose — see the pressed entry. The resting state is a neutral surface, which is the whole point: it is what makes the press mean something.

components.name: SM-2 Rating Button — pressed
components.description: The commitment moment. Because the resting state is neutral, the solid state fill is the only saturated thing in the row and reads unambiguously as a choice being made.
components.notes: No :hover rule, deliberately. The base .ratingBtn:hover (--surface-2 + accent border) is dead code in the real stylesheet — the per-grade :hover at higher specificity always wins, so a rating button goes straight from resting to the solid state fill. The two entries above are the two states that actually exist.

components.name: Level Chip — active
components.description: The single solid accent surface on the study screen. It marks the active filter and nothing else; the rating row is deliberately neutral so this keeps that meaning.
components.css: .ds-level { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-width:44px; min-height:44px; border-radius:var(--radius-pill); background:var(--accent-solid); color:var(--accent-fg); font-family:var(--font-sans); font-size:var(--text-small); font-weight:600; }
components.notes: A <span>, not a control: it renders the active filter and is not itself interactive, so it has no hover or focus state. This is the only solid accent surface on the study screen.

components.name: Chip — filter, unselected
components.description: Filter chips sit on a tinted ground with muted ink. They never compete with the active level chip for attention.

components.name: Flashcard
components.description: The study object. Opaque from frame one, lifted by a warm offset shadow — a page set down on a desk, not an overlay fading in. The Kazakh word is the only place the display serif is used at size.
components.html:

яблоко сладкое.

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Focus swaps the hairline to the accent and adds a soft ring; :focus-visible adds the outline so keyboard and pointer focus look identical.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="search" placeholder="Поиск…" aria-label="Поиск по словам">
components.notes: No :hover, matching the real stylesheet. A form field that changes on hover is noise; focus is the only state a field has.

components.name: Navigation — link
components.description: Topbar links at body-small. The active link is a filled pill on the inset ground with strong ink — a tonal shift, not a colour one.
components.html: Главная

components.name: Collapsed filter row — study
components.description: Compact-only. One 44px row that names the three active filter values instead of showing the three labelled selects, and opens the full stack on tap. The three rows are 187px; this is 44px. The form-field reading is unchanged — it is a height decision, not a quieting one.
components.notes: The summary must keep naming the three active values. Collapsing that hides the controls, not the state they hold — a row of three words is the whole disclosure label.

narrative.overview: Warm, paper-grounded, editorial. The system is built to read like a well-typeset study notebook rather than an app: a warm cream ground, a serif face held in reserve for the Kazakh word, and one terracotta accent that has to earn every appearance. Density is a feature — this is a 3,996-word dictionary with a stats page full of meters, and the compactness was tuned deliberately at a 15px root — but density and noise are not the same thing. The product has no gradients, no glass, no glow, no gamification, and no decorative illustration; the personality lives in the warmth of the ground, the restraint of the accent, and the typographic contrast between the language the learner knows and the language they are learning.
keyCharacteristics: One warm ground, one accent, and a documented refusal to let either grow.
A serif that appears only where the learner is meeting the new language.
Colour identity lives on a keyline and a label; area belongs to the work.
Token discipline: every value is a named role, never a literal.
The reduced-motion path is per-component and intentional, never a blanket.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Fill Rule
rules.body: Text never sits on bare --accent or bare --warn. Split the role: --accent-solid + --accent-fg.

rules.name: The One-Area Rule
rules.body: When a product has one accent and a semantic scale, check whether the scale is borrowing the accent. --easy-* reuses the accent role, so any large surface in that state silently competes with every CTA in the app. Colour identity belongs on a keyline and a label; area belongs to the one thing the screen is for.

rules.name: The Commitment Rule
rules.body: Solid fill is not a resting style. It marks the moment the learner commits. A control that is already saturated at rest has nothing left to give the press.

rules.name: The Never-px Rule
rules.body: Never set a font size in px. px does not follow --font-scale, so a px shorthand silently opts that element out of the user's text-size setting.

rules.name: The Root-Size Rule
rules.body: Root is 15px, not the 16px web default. The density was deliberately tuned at 15px, and the sm setting is clamped to 0.92× so the compact step cannot drive the smallest role below ~10.8px. Raising the root is a whole-product proportion change, not a side effect of a cleanup.

rules.name: The Offset-and-Blur Rule
rules.body: No zero-offset coloured halos, no hard offset shadows. Both are costume, not a depth system.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface earns its shadow by being a floating object (a card, a modal), not by existing.

dos: Use the token ramp for every font size, duration, curve, radius, colour, and shadow. If a value has no token, that is a finding.
Put text on --accent-solid / --accent-fg as a pair, never on bare --accent.
Keep colour identity on a keyline and a label, and let a large area be reserved for the one thing the screen is for.
Give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion alternative in the same file, written as an intentional substitute rather than a duration of zero.
Pair a hover affordance with :focus-visible and a @media (hover: none) fallback.
Verify contrast after changing a token, in both themes.
Use 62ch for sustained prose and text-wrap: balance on headings.
donts: Don't reference a token that is not defined in src/styles/global.css.
Don't add a blanket reduced-motion rule. It removes feedback, and feedback is information.
Don't reintroduce the SM-2 tinted resting surface.
Don't use a coloured border-left/border-right above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism as decoration, hard offset shadows, or zero-offset coloured halos.
Don't use a system display face, or monospace as a costume for 'technical'.
Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as an icon system.
Don't animate a layout-driving property when a transform will do.
Don't ship a study screen where the answer widget is the most prominent thing on the page.
Don't desaturate the palette in pursuit of quiet. Quieter is not greyer.
Don't flatten the study filter stack to save visual weight.
